lesson_title: The Machine That Cannot Decide: Functions and Inverses
hook_text: A vending machine that drops TWO snacks for one code is broken. Run it backwards and you meet the most examined trap in the functions topic.
clip_script: Picture a vending machine. Punch in a code, exactly one snack falls. That is a function: one input, one output, no exceptions. Now run the machine backwards — you hold the snack and ask which code produced it. For y equals 3 x minus 5 the reverse is easy: swap x and y, solve, done. But throw y equals x squared into reverse and the machine stalls. You hold the snack 16 and it cannot decide: maybe the code was 4, maybe minus 4. Two codes bought the same snack, so the reversal answers with plus or minus — and a machine that offers choices is not a function. The early warning is a horizontal line on the original graph: touch it twice and the reverse will stall. The fix is surgery: disconnect half the machine. Keep only codes x greater than or equal to zero, and the right arm of the parabola reverses cleanly into the square root of x. One arm at a time, every parabola becomes reversible. Mirror across the diagonal, horizontal line to predict the stall, one arm to fix it.
visual_style: A neon vending machine dropping snacks along a forty-five degree mirror line, a parabola splitting into two glowing arms, one arm powering down while the other reverses smoothly.
pacing: Quick setup on the working machine, a jolt at the stall on 16, steady confidence through the one-arm fix.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make any function run backwards without stalling.
